I read the whole file (lines 1–149). Every theorem is a single `decide +kernel` call. No proof contains nontrivial reasoning that is written out twice, so there is no proof body to factor into a shared lemma.

The file does repeat statement shapes: closure, inverse, normality, bound and length checks for g22R1Idx and g22R2Idx, and the paired qA/qB checks. I considered introducing a predicate such as "index list closed under compL" with a generic lemma. That would only restate the same kernel-decided facts. It would not remove any repeated mathematical argument, and it would likely cost more kernel evaluation or elaboration. The rubric excludes short calculations, routine unfolding and thin wrappers, so I did not report it.

I did not check how downstream files use these checks. Any such use would not change the verdict for this file.
